evidence: Plaut. Cas. fin.: manibus clārē (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Manibus plaudere, to clap one’s hands; alicui plaudere, to clap for someone. The comedies end on plaudite.

terms.gloss: clap the hands together, in joy or dismay
evidence: Quint. 11.3.123: complōdere manūs scaenicum est (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Post-Augustan prose; Quintilian calls it a gesture for the stage.

phrases.latin: salit, cadit, rīdet, iterum salit, dum Baba juxtā plaudit
phrases.english: he jumps, falls, laughs, jumps again, while Baba claps beside him
Clap your hands, all you nations
Goodbye, and give us a clap.

sources: Lewis & Short: plaudo · Lewis & Short: complodo
